annotations.text:
WHAT'S WRONG NOW

Seven .panel boxes with identical 1px borders — chart, standing, allocation, trades, positions all the same visual weight. Nothing is more important than anything else, so the eye has nowhere to land.

And on a page about a person, the person is the smallest thing on it: an 11px handle and a letter in a circle.

Each direction below attacks a different axis.

A — PLAYER CARD

The person becomes the hero. 40px name, rank as a gold medallion, value at 46px. The curve bleeds edge to edge as the page's spine, and the stats drop their boxes for a hairline band.

Why: it's a profile — its job is to make someone's standing feel like something worth sharing.

Tradeoff: the most 'designed' of the three, so it's the furthest from the rest of the app and the most work to keep consistent.

B — TERMINAL READOUT

No rounded panels anywhere. Hairline rules only, everything mono, tight rows, a real price axis, a TOTAL line, a blotter. Colour appears only as signal.

Why: you keep asking for it to feel real. This is what a trading screen actually looks like, and it's nothing like a generic dark dashboard.

Tradeoff: cold and dense. Reads as a tool, not a place — and a shared profile is arguably a place.

C — EDITORIAL

One 68px number and a full-bleed curve carry the page. Almost no borders — space does the separating. Sans for names, mono only for numerals.

Why: calm and premium, and the easiest to read at a glance.

Tradeoff: it's the Robinhood/Linear look. Handsome, but it doesn't say 'stock terminal', and it's the least distinctive of the three.

WHY THE PALETTE READS FLAT

Measured on the colours in tailwind.config.ts:

1. The surfaces barely differ. bg→panel is 1.04:1, panel→raise 1.06:1, raise→line 1.12:1. A panel is essentially invisible AS a surface — the 1px border is doing 100% of the structural work. That is the wireframe feeling, and no amount of layout fixes it.

2. Every neutral is the same hue. bg 218°, panel 220°, raise 220°, line 220°, muted 215°, text 216°. Six colours, one hue, so nothing recedes and nothing advances — the screen is a flat sheet.

3. The accents are stock Tailwind. #22c55e is green-500, #f43f5e is rose-500, #38bdf8 is sky-400, #fbbf24 is amber-400. That is the default dark-dashboard palette, which is exactly what it looks like.

All three alternatives below widen the surface steps and drop the defaults. Same UI slice in each, so only the colour differs.

WHAT READS AS AMATEUR (all counted in the repo, not guessed)

1. Mood lighting. A green radial glow sits behind every page (globals.css, rgba(34,197,94,0.07)). Serious instruments have flat backgrounds; a glow is a landing-page move.

2. The label style, 58 times. Every section header is 10px uppercase mono at 0.18em tracking. Once it is a nice detail; 58 times it is the signature of a dark-dashboard template — and it is genuinely hard to read at 10px.

3. Low density. Rows are ~53px for one line of data. Instruments run 28-32px. Fitting twice the information is itself what capability looks like — and right now a five-position book does not fill a screen.

4. A pill on every number. 32 tinted chips for percentage changes. Colour the digits instead; pills are a consumer-app habit and they fight the table's alignment.

5. Jokes where facts go. "building your tape…", "the tape starts when someone pulls the trigger", "All cash, no conviction — yet", "Movers in your book". Each is fine alone; together they cost authority. A professional tool says "Marked 18:04:11 ET".

6. No units, no totals. Every cell repeats the $. Real tables state the unit once in the header, fix the decimals, right-align, and foot the columns with a total.

7. 10px radii everywhere. Friendly. 4px reads like an instrument.

Middle board is the treatment ALONE on the current palette — which is most of the distance. Right board adds Ink.
